mathematical_interface_arguments.qmd_to_dqm: At an interior point, fixed v!=0 admits theta0+tv for all sufficiently small |t|. Substitute h=tv: the norm remainder is o(|t| ||v||)=o(|t|), with scalar score v^T s square-integrable by Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz. Restrict t>=0. v=0 gives the constant path. This one-ray restriction does not assert the converse vector-QMD condition or allow negative directions at constrained boundaries.
mathematical_interface_arguments.centering: Vector QMD assumes finite second moments but not centering; current batch23 lemma derives E s=0 from the squared root-density normalization. Batch28 scalar DQM uses the same normalization and subtracts expansions to establish score uniqueness. Full AC for density versions is explicit; no common exceptional null set is assumed.
mathematical_interface_arguments.pathwise_and_representation: The pathwise definition requires the right derivative on every allowed path to depend only on its score and extend continuously to the closed real tangent span. Under Countable Choice, Riesz supplies a unique tangent-space representer. Two ambient representers differ by an orthogonal-complement vector; projecting one gives the unique tangent representative. These statements do not depend on LAN or claim existence of an efficient estimator.
mathematical_interface_arguments.efficient_score: The current theorem requires the EXACT designated allowed score set S={a^T S_theta+t}, its closed span T, closed nuisance T_eta, right derivative a on EVERY allowed path, AC/Countable Choice and nonsingular I_eff. Orthogonality gives E[S_eff S_theta^T]=I_eff; nonsingularity makes the coefficient a well-defined; phi=I_eff^-1 S_eff continuously represents derivatives and has covariance I_eff^-1. No absent page theorem is used.
mathematical_interface_arguments.estimator_definition: Asymptotic linearity is a measurable expansion with centered square-integrable estimator influence function. The definition explicitly makes no local-regularity, pathwise-differentiability or asymptotic-normality assertion.
mathematical_interface_arguments.examples: Bounded centered tilts have square-root remainder O(t²), and centered truncations are dense. For the finite-variance mean, X-mu continuously represents the derivative and the sample-mean expansion is exact. For masses c k^-3, E X finite and E X² infinite; centered truncated scores have derivative-to-norm ratio diverging like sqrt(log m), so no finite-variance representer exists. The four-point finite model has scores U+V and U, projection U and efficient score/canonical gradient V, with all allowed straight-path derivative hypotheses verified.
